collection.name: IELTS Vocabulary by Band
collection.description: Advanced IELTS vocabulary grouped by target band score (4.0–8.0+). POS + IPA + Vietnamese meaning.

meta.note: Claude-authored enrichment (no external LLM). difficulty derived from the curated set's own CEFR/IELTS bands. Vietnamese meanings verified/corrected on enriched rows.

words.vi_meaning: giải thích chi tiết, làm rõ
words.definition_en: to explain an idea or text in careful, detailed terms
words.example_simple: The teacher took time to explicate the difficult poem for us.
words.example_complex: In her lecture, the professor sought to explicate the subtle contradictions embedded within the philosopher's central argument.

words.definition_en: to reach a final, climactic point or result after a process
words.example_simple: Months of hard work culminated in a wonderful graduation ceremony.
words.example_complex: Decades of unchecked emissions may culminate in irreversible ecological consequences that future generations will struggle to reverse.

words.definition_en: to change completely into a different form or nature
words.example_simple: The caterpillar will slowly metamorphose into a beautiful butterfly.
words.example_complex: Under sustained economic pressure, the quiet fishing village metamorphosed into a bustling industrial hub within a single generation.

words.definition_en: in a way that leaves no doubt; clearly and absolutely
words.example_simple: She unequivocally told us that she would not change her mind.
words.example_complex: The committee unequivocally condemned the policy, stressing that no exceptions could justify such a breach of ethics.

words.definition_en: a system of ideas and beliefs guiding a group or movement
words.example_simple: Their political ideology shaped how they voted in the election.
words.example_complex: The revolution was driven less by material hardship than by an ideology promising radical social equality.

words.definition_en: a stable equilibrium among species and their natural environment
words.example_simple: Cutting down too many trees can upset the ecological balance of the forest.
words.example_complex: Introducing a non-native predator often shatters the ecological balance that has evolved over millennia.

words.definition_en: the deterioration of the natural environment through pollution or overuse
words.example_simple: Factories that dump waste into rivers add to environmental degradation.
words.example_complex: Rampant deforestation and industrial runoff have accelerated environmental degradation across the once-fertile delta.

words.definition_en: in an original, unspoiled, and perfectly clean condition
words.example_simple: The mountain lake was so pristine that we could see the bottom.
words.example_complex: Conservationists fought to keep the arctic tundra pristine, wary of the damage even minimal tourism might inflict.

words.definition_en: teaching that develops the whole person, not just academic ability
words.example_simple: The school offers holistic education, focusing on both grades and emotional growth.
words.example_complex: Advocates of holistic education argue that nurturing creativity and empathy is as vital as cultivating measurable academic outcomes.

words.definition_en: the approaches and techniques used for teaching and instruction
words.example_simple: New pedagogical methods make lessons more interactive for young students.
words.example_complex: Researchers evaluated whether learner-centred pedagogical methods yield deeper comprehension than conventional lecturing.

words.vi_meaning: nuôi dưỡng sự tò mò trí tuệ
words.definition_en: to nurture and encourage a genuine desire to learn and question
words.example_simple: Good teachers cultivate intellectual curiosity by asking open-ended questions.
words.example_complex: Universities should cultivate intellectual curiosity rather than merely rewarding students for memorising prescribed answers.

words.vi_meaning: sự thay đổi nhân khẩu học
words.definition_en: changes in the composition or distribution of a population
words.example_simple: Demographic shifts mean many towns now have far more elderly residents.
words.example_complex: Policymakers must anticipate demographic shifts, as an ageing workforce places mounting strain on pension systems.

words.definition_en: a shared sense of belonging and self-definition within a group
words.example_simple: Cheering for the same team gave the fans a strong collective identity.
words.example_complex: Migration and globalisation can erode a nation's collective identity while simultaneously forging new, hybrid allegiances.

words.definition_en: the process of absorbing individuals or ideas into a dominant group
words.example_simple: Learning the local language helped their assimilation into the new country.
words.example_complex: Debates over immigration frequently pit assimilation against the preservation of distinct cultural traditions.

words.definition_en: shortages of essential nutrients needed for good health
words.example_simple: A diet lacking fruit can lead to nutritional deficiencies like low vitamin C.
words.example_complex: Persistent nutritional deficiencies in early childhood can impair cognitive development well into adulthood.

words.definition_en: to make the signs of an illness less severe or painful
words.example_simple: Drinking warm tea can alleviate symptoms of a sore throat.
words.example_complex: While the drug does not cure the condition, it markedly alleviates symptoms and improves patients' quality of life.

words.definition_en: a central bank's control of money supply and interest rates
words.example_simple: The bank changed its monetary policy to keep prices from rising too fast.
words.example_complex: By tightening monetary policy, the central bank hoped to curb inflation without triggering a sharp rise in unemployment.

words.definition_en: the point where a product's demand is fully met, limiting sales growth
words.example_simple: With everyone owning a smartphone, the market saturation slowed new sales.
words.example_complex: Facing market saturation at home, the corporation pivoted aggressively toward emerging economies to sustain revenue growth.

words.definition_en: a period of significant decline in economic activity and output
words.example_simple: Many people lost their jobs during the economic recession.
words.example_complex: The prolonged economic recession forced governments to adopt unprecedented stimulus measures to stabilise faltering markets.

words.definition_en: the suppression of speech, media, or information deemed objectionable
words.example_simple: Because of censorship, some films were never shown in that country.
words.example_complex: State censorship of the press undermines democratic accountability by shielding those in power from public scrutiny.

words.definition_en: large or important enough to have a noticeable effect
words.example_simple: There was a significant rise in the number of visitors this year.
words.example_complex: The study revealed a significant correlation between sleep deprivation and diminished academic performance.

words.definition_en: a demanding task or situation that tests one's abilities
words.example_simple: Learning a new language was a real challenge for him at first.
words.example_complex: Climate change poses perhaps the most formidable challenge humanity has ever confronted collectively.

words.definition_en: natural fuels such as coal, oil, and gas formed from ancient organisms
words.example_simple: Cars that burn fossil fuels release gases into the air.
words.example_complex: Weaning industrialised economies off fossil fuels remains essential if global warming is to be kept within safe limits.

words.definition_en: the variety of living species within a particular habitat or ecosystem
words.example_simple: Rainforests have amazing biodiversity, with thousands of plants and animals.
words.example_complex: The wetland's remarkable biodiversity makes its conservation a priority for scientists studying ecosystem resilience.

words.definition_en: growth that meets present needs without harming future generations
words.example_simple: Sustainable development means using resources carefully so they last.
words.example_complex: Balancing economic expansion with environmental stewardship lies at the heart of any genuine sustainable development strategy.

words.definition_en: instruction that teaches practical skills for a specific trade or job
words.example_simple: He chose vocational training to become an electrician instead of university.
words.example_complex: Expanding vocational training could ease youth unemployment by aligning workers' skills with the demands of local industry.

words.definition_en: the ability to understand and work confidently with numbers
words.example_simple: Good numeracy helps you manage money and check your change.
words.example_complex: Low levels of adult numeracy can limit employment prospects and hinder informed financial decision-making.

words.definition_en: computer systems able to perform tasks that normally require human thought
words.example_simple: Artificial intelligence helps my phone recognise my face.
words.example_complex: As artificial intelligence permeates the workplace, questions about accountability and job displacement grow ever more pressing.

words.definition_en: improvements and breakthroughs in technology over time
words.example_simple: Technological advancements have made phones much faster than before.
words.example_complex: Rapid technological advancements in medicine have transformed once-fatal diagnoses into manageable chronic conditions.

words.definition_en: the transmission of information over distances by electronic means
words.example_simple: Telecommunication lets us call friends who live far away.
words.example_complex: The expansion of telecommunication infrastructure has connected remote communities to global markets and services.

words.definition_en: a problem that affects many people within a society
words.example_simple: Homelessness is a serious social issue in many big cities.
words.example_complex: Politicians who ignore deep-rooted social issues risk fostering the very unrest they hope to avoid.

words.definition_en: an unfair difference in wealth, status, or opportunity between people
words.example_simple: There is still a lot of inequality between rich and poor families.
words.example_complex: Widening income inequality can erode social cohesion and fuel resentment toward established institutions.

words.definition_en: the growing interconnection of the world's economies and cultures
words.example_simple: Because of globalization, we can buy products from all over the world.
words.example_complex: Globalization has lifted millions out of poverty, yet it has also deepened the gulf between winners and losers of open markets.

words.definition_en: the coexistence and acceptance of diverse cultures within one society
words.example_simple: The city's multiculturalism means you can taste food from many countries.
words.example_complex: Proponents of multiculturalism contend that cultural diversity enriches a nation's intellectual and creative life.

words.definition_en: the legal status of belonging to a country, with its rights and duties
words.example_simple: After living there for years, she finally gained citizenship.
words.example_complex: Active citizenship entails not merely holding rights but also shouldering responsibilities toward one's community.

words.definition_en: The likelihood or opportunities of being advanced to a higher position at work.
words.example_simple: She took the new job because it offered better promotion prospects.
words.example_complex: Employees frequently cite stagnant promotion prospects as a leading reason for seeking alternative employment elsewhere.

words.definition_en: The abilities needed to guide, motivate, and manage a group of people effectively.
words.example_simple: Playing team sports helped him build his leadership skills from an early age.
words.example_complex: The programme is designed to cultivate the leadership skills that graduates will require in increasingly collaborative workplaces.

words.definition_en: The loss of a job because the employer no longer needs the position.
words.example_simple: Many workers were worried about redundancy when the factory closed.
words.example_complex: The wave of redundancies that followed the merger disproportionately affected long-serving administrative staff.

words.definition_en: Any bodily movement produced by muscles that uses energy, such as exercise.
words.example_simple: Doctors recommend at least thirty minutes of physical activity each day.
words.example_complex: Longitudinal studies consistently link sustained physical activity with reduced incidence of cardiovascular disease in later life.

words.vi_meaning: công nghệ mang tính đột phá
words.definition_en: New technology that significantly changes or displaces an established industry or market.
words.example_simple: Smartphones were a disruptive technology that changed how people communicate.
words.example_complex: Incumbent firms often underestimate disruptive technologies precisely because they initially serve only niche, low-margin segments.

words.definition_en: A proposed explanation put forward as a starting point for further investigation.
words.example_simple: The scientists ran experiments to test their hypothesis.
words.example_complex: The data gathered over five years neither conclusively confirmed nor refuted the researchers' central hypothesis.

words.vi_meaning: vô lương tâm, bất chấp thủ đoạn
words.definition_en: Having no moral principles; behaving in a dishonest or unfair way.
words.example_simple: The unscrupulous salesman lied to customers to make more money.
words.example_complex: Regulators introduced stricter oversight to protect vulnerable consumers from unscrupulous lenders exploiting legal loopholes.

words.definition_en: Putting a lot of effort and diligence into one's work or tasks.
words.example_simple: She is a hard-working student who never misses a deadline.
words.example_complex: The company's success is largely attributable to a hard-working team that consistently exceeds performance targets.

words.definition_en: Comfortable, informal clothing suitable for relaxed, everyday occasions.
words.example_simple: On weekends he prefers casual wear like jeans and a T-shirt.
words.example_complex: The relaxed dress code allows employees to adopt casual wear, provided it remains presentable for client meetings.

words.definition_en: Smart, elegant clothing worn for official or ceremonial occasions.
words.example_simple: The wedding invitation asked all guests to arrive in formal wear.
words.example_complex: Diplomatic functions typically demand formal wear, signalling both respect and adherence to established protocol.

words.definition_en: The degree to which a person is physically healthy and able to exercise.
words.example_simple: Running every morning has really improved my fitness level.
words.example_complex: The training regimen is tailored to each participant's fitness level to minimise the risk of injury.

words.definition_en: The tools, machines, or supplies needed for a particular purpose or activity.
words.example_simple: The gym has all the equipment you need for a good workout.
words.example_complex: Researchers require sophisticated laboratory equipment to detect concentrations of the compound at the molecular level.

words.definition_en: A competition involving many players or teams competing in a series of games.
words.example_simple: Our school team reached the final of the football tournament.
words.example_complex: The prestigious tournament attracts elite athletes whose performances are scrutinised by scouts from around the world.

words.definition_en: Showing intense and eager enjoyment, interest, or approval about something.
words.example_simple: The children were enthusiastic about the trip to the zoo.
words.example_complex: Her enthusiastic endorsement of the reforms galvanised colleagues who had previously been reluctant to change.

words.definition_en: Confident and forceful in stating one's opinions or claims respectfully.
words.example_simple: You need to be more assertive when asking for a pay rise.
words.example_complex: An assertive negotiating style, distinct from aggression, allowed her to secure favourable terms without alienating partners.

words.definition_en: Behaving in an unusual or slightly strange way that differs from the norm.
words.example_simple: My uncle is a bit eccentric and collects old clocks.
words.example_complex: The novelist's eccentric habits, once dismissed as affectation, later came to be seen as integral to his creative process.

words.definition_en: A place to live, stay, or work in, especially temporarily.
words.example_simple: We booked our accommodation online before the trip.
words.example_complex: The influx of tourists has driven up demand for short-term accommodation across the historic city centre.

words.definition_en: A business that arranges trips, tickets, and holidays for travellers.
words.example_simple: We used a travel agency to plan our holiday to Italy.
words.example_complex: Traditional travel agencies have had to reinvent themselves as consumers increasingly book itineraries directly online.

words.definition_en: Knowledge or skill gained over time; also, to encounter or undergo something.
words.example_simple: She has years of experience working with children.
words.example_complex: Candidates who have experienced diverse working environments tend to adapt more readily to organisational change.

words.definition_en: The activity of visiting interesting places, especially as a tourist.
words.example_simple: We spent the morning sightseeing around the old town.
words.example_complex: Beyond conventional sightseeing, the itinerary encouraged travellers to engage meaningfully with local communities and customs.

words.definition_en: A style or method of cooking, especially of a particular country or region.
words.example_simple: I love trying different cuisines when I travel abroad.
words.example_complex: The region's cuisine reflects centuries of trade, blending indigenous ingredients with flavours introduced by foreign settlers.

words.definition_en: A district or area within a town or city where people live.
words.example_simple: They moved to a friendly neighbourhood near the park.
words.example_complex: Urban regeneration transformed a once-neglected neighbourhood into a thriving hub for artists and small businesses.

words.definition_en: The system of money used in a particular country or economic area.
words.example_simple: You should exchange your currency before you travel.
words.example_complex: A sudden depreciation of the national currency eroded household savings and heightened political instability.

words.definition_en: A person who shows tourists around places and explains their history.
words.example_simple: Our tour guide told us fascinating stories about the castle.
words.example_complex: An experienced tour guide can transform a routine visit into a vivid, immersive encounter with the past.

words.definition_en: A person who makes and repairs wooden objects and structures.
words.example_simple: The carpenter built us a beautiful oak table.
words.example_complex: A master carpenter's precision joinery, achieved without nails, testifies to a craft refined over generations.

words.definition_en: The general weather conditions of a place over a long period.
words.example_simple: The country has a warm climate all year round.
words.example_complex: Shifting rainfall patterns associated with a changing climate threaten the viability of traditional agriculture in the region.

words.definition_en: All the visible features of an area of countryside or land.
words.example_simple: The mountain landscape was breathtaking at sunrise.
words.example_complex: Centuries of intensive farming have profoundly reshaped a landscape once dominated by dense ancient woodland.

words.definition_en: Tending to expect the worst possible outcome in any situation.
words.example_simple: He was pessimistic about passing the exam.
words.example_complex: Economists offered a strikingly pessimistic forecast, warning that recovery would be slower than official projections suggested.

words.definition_en: A group of people related by blood, marriage, or close bonds.
words.example_simple: We spend every holiday with our whole family.
words.example_complex: Sociologists note that the traditional nuclear family is increasingly one arrangement among many diverse household structures.

words.definition_en: A person connected to another by blood or marriage; a family member.
words.example_simple: Several relatives came to celebrate my grandmother's birthday.
words.example_complex: Genealogical databases now allow individuals to identify distant relatives they had no prior knowledge of.

words.definition_en: A living organism that feeds on organic matter and can move independently.
words.example_simple: The children love visiting the animals at the farm.
words.example_complex: Conservationists warn that many animal species face extinction as their natural habitats are steadily destroyed.

words.definition_en: A book or resource listing words with their meanings and usage.
words.example_simple: I looked up the new word in my dictionary.
words.example_complex: Lexicographers continually revise the dictionary to document neologisms and shifts in established usage.

words.definition_en: A book used for studying a particular subject, especially in school.
words.example_simple: Please open your textbook to page fifty.
words.example_complex: Critics argue that outdated textbooks can perpetuate misconceptions long after scholarship has moved on.

words.definition_en: A cold, non-alcoholic drink, usually sweet and often carbonated.
words.example_simple: She ordered a soft drink instead of coffee.
words.example_complex: Public health campaigns increasingly target soft drink consumption as a significant contributor to childhood obesity.

words.definition_en: The study of human society, including history, geography, and civics.
words.example_simple: We learned about local government in our social studies class.
words.example_complex: A well-designed social studies curriculum equips students to interpret contemporary issues within their broader historical context.

words.definition_en: To acquire the ability to understand and communicate in foreign tongues.
words.example_simple: She loves to learn languages, and she already speaks three of them.
words.example_complex: Immersion abroad remains the most effective way to learn languages, since constant exposure accelerates both fluency and cultural understanding.

words.definition_en: To gather and keep postage stamps as an organised hobby.
words.example_simple: My grandfather likes to collect stamps from every country he visits.
words.example_complex: Enthusiasts who collect stamps often argue that philately preserves miniature records of a nation's political and artistic history.

words.definition_en: To pay attention to sounds arranged as songs or compositions.
words.example_simple: I like to listen to music while I do my homework.
words.example_complex: Recent studies suggest that people who regularly listen to music while working may experience reduced stress but occasionally diminished concentration.

words.definition_en: A signal with coloured lights controlling the movement of vehicles.
words.example_simple: You must stop your car when the traffic light turns red.
words.example_complex: Smart traffic lights that adjust to real-time congestion could substantially cut the emissions produced by idling vehicles at busy intersections.

words.definition_en: A building or place where buses start, stop, and pick up passengers.
words.example_simple: We met our friends at the bus station before the trip.
words.example_complex: The modernised bus station now integrates rail and cycling links, reflecting a broader push toward seamless urban public transport.

words.definition_en: Feeling awkward, ashamed, or uncomfortable in a social situation.
words.example_simple: He was embarrassed when he forgot his teacher's name.
words.example_complex: Visibly embarrassed by the auditor's findings, the executive struggled to defend the discrepancies before the assembled shareholders.

words.definition_en: A person trained to travel and work in outer space.
words.example_simple: The young boy dreams of becoming an astronaut one day.
words.example_complex: Every astronaut endures years of rigorous physiological and psychological conditioning before being cleared for a long-duration orbital mission.

words.definition_en: A performer whose job is to entertain people by making them laugh.
words.example_simple: The comedian told so many jokes that everyone laughed all night.
words.example_complex: A skilled comedian weaves social commentary into humour, disarming audiences even as they confront uncomfortable truths.

words.definition_en: A person who starts and manages a business, taking financial risks.
words.example_simple: The young entrepreneur opened her first coffee shop last year.
words.example_complex: A visionary entrepreneur must balance calculated risk-taking with disciplined financial management to sustain a venture through volatile markets.

words.definition_en: Energetically busy, involved, or physically and mentally lively.
words.example_simple: My grandmother is still very active and walks every morning.
words.example_complex: Remaining cognitively active in later life appears to delay the onset of degenerative conditions such as dementia.

words.definition_en: Careful, thorough, and diligent in doing one's work or duty.
words.example_simple: She is a conscientious student who always finishes her work on time.
words.example_complex: Conscientious employees, who consistently attend to detail, tend to outperform more talented but careless colleagues over the long term.

words.definition_en: A software program, or a formal request, or a practical use of something.
words.example_simple: I downloaded a new application to help me learn vocabulary.
words.example_complex: The practical application of this theory in industrial settings has transformed how engineers approach material fatigue.

words.definition_en: A scientific test done to discover or prove something.
words.example_simple: We did an experiment in class to see how plants grow.
words.example_complex: The experiment was carefully controlled to isolate the single variable responsible for the observed change in reaction rate.

words.definition_en: Using or preferring very simple, sparse design with few elements.
words.example_simple: Her bedroom has a minimalist style with just a bed and a lamp.
words.example_complex: The architect's minimalist approach stripped the interior to its essentials, letting light and proportion carry the entire aesthetic.

words.definition_en: A violent tropical storm with strong winds, common in the Pacific.
words.example_simple: The typhoon brought heavy rain and knocked down many trees.
words.example_complex: As the typhoon intensified overnight, coastal authorities ordered mass evacuations to avert the devastating storm surge.

words.definition_en: A prediction of future conditions, especially the weather.
words.example_simple: The weather forecast says it will rain tomorrow afternoon.
words.example_complex: The bank's gloomy economic forecast prompted investors to withdraw capital from emerging markets almost overnight.

words.definition_en: A person who is paid to work for a company or organisation.
words.example_simple: Every employee at the shop wears a blue uniform.
words.example_complex: The firm's decision to reward each employee with equity dramatically improved retention among its most skilled engineers.

words.definition_en: Having a duty to deal with something, or being reliable and trustworthy.
words.example_simple: She is responsible for feeding the class rabbit every day.
words.example_complex: Managers held directly responsible for safety lapses are far more likely to enforce rigorous compliance procedures.

words.definition_en: A room or building equipped for scientific experiments and research.
words.example_simple: The students put on gloves before entering the laboratory.
words.example_complex: The pharmaceutical laboratory operates under strict sterile protocols to prevent any contamination of its sensitive cultures.

words.definition_en: To generate many ideas quickly through free group discussion.
words.example_simple: Let's brainstorm some ideas for the school party.
words.example_complex: During the workshop, participants brainstorm freely before critically evaluating which proposals merit further development.

words.definition_en: To work jointly with others to achieve a shared goal.
words.example_simple: The two classes will collaborate to make a big wall poster.
words.example_complex: When researchers from different disciplines collaborate, they frequently uncover insights that neither field could have reached alone.

words.definition_en: A special event or activity held to mark a happy occasion.
words.example_simple: There was a big celebration in the village after the harvest.
words.example_complex: The centenary celebration blended traditional ritual with contemporary performance, drawing visitors from across the region.

words.definition_en: The way that someone or something looks to others.
words.example_simple: He always cares about his appearance before going out.
words.example_complex: The company insists that a candidate's competence, not their appearance, should determine hiring decisions.

words.definition_en: A person who greets and helps visitors at an office or hotel.
words.example_simple: The receptionist gave us the key to our hotel room.
words.example_complex: A courteous receptionist often shapes a client's first impression more decisively than any marketing campaign.

words.definition_en: Fish and shellfish from the sea that are eaten as food.
words.example_simple: We ate delicious seafood by the beach last summer.
words.example_complex: Rising ocean temperatures threaten the seafood supply chains upon which many coastal economies depend.

words.definition_en: A place where books and other resources are kept for reading and borrowing.
words.example_simple: I borrowed three books from the library yesterday.
words.example_complex: The university library has digitised its rare manuscripts, granting scholars worldwide unprecedented access to fragile historical texts.

words.definition_en: A mobile phone with advanced computing and internet features.
words.example_simple: She uses her smartphone to take photos and send messages.
words.example_complex: Excessive smartphone use before bedtime has been repeatedly linked to disrupted sleep patterns among adolescents.

words.definition_en: A regularly published booklet with articles, pictures, and advertisements.
words.example_simple: My mother reads a cooking magazine every weekend.
words.example_complex: As print advertising declined, the magazine reinvented itself as a subscription-based digital platform to survive.

words.definition_en: School work that pupils are given to do at home.
words.example_simple: I have to finish my maths homework before dinner.
words.example_complex: Educators continue to debate whether heavy homework loads genuinely reinforce learning or merely heighten student anxiety.

words.definition_en: A custom or belief passed down through generations within a group.
words.example_simple: Eating cake on your birthday is a popular tradition.
words.example_complex: Preserving an ancient tradition while adapting it to modern values is a delicate task for any community.

words.definition_en: Firmly faithful and devoted to a person, group, or cause.
words.example_simple: A loyal dog will always wait for its owner.
words.example_complex: Brands invest heavily in rewards programmes because a loyal customer base insulates revenue against competitive disruption.

words.definition_en: A large area of land thickly covered with trees and plants.
words.example_simple: We saw many birds when we walked through the forest.
words.example_complex: Clearing the rainforest for agriculture releases vast quantities of stored carbon, accelerating global climate change.

words.definition_en: A mountain with an opening through which lava and gases erupt.
words.example_simple: The volcano sent smoke and ash high into the sky.
words.example_complex: Geologists monitor the dormant volcano constantly, since even subtle seismic tremors may signal an impending eruption.

words.definition_en: The activity of buying goods from shops or online stores.
words.example_simple: We went shopping for new clothes at the mall.
words.example_complex: The explosive growth of online shopping has hollowed out traditional high streets across much of the developed world.
